status: Implemented; default, Worker and explicit HTTP stateful-sort validation passed
change: sortWithState owns detached restored and newly scanned rows through checkpoint processing. Run construction admits copied directories and native-sort scratch. Merge admits cursor/heap storage sized by run count and its output directory sized by total rows. Temporary current-run directories are disposed after each flush; parent ownership is released on every exit.

cases: scanner object reuse across one-row runs
validation.followup: Twelve focused stateful-sort tests passed after adding asynchronous spill rejection: row ownership stays live while write is pending and cleanup preserves sibling ownership.
validation.remoteEvidence: Real wide-timestamp Parquet over HTTP 206 and ignored-range 200, row-only scanner, four concurrent sortWithState queries with maxBufferedRows=2. Result parity, nonempty checkpoints, bounded pool peak and final zero usage verified. Timestamp checkpoint restoration is not claimed by this fixture.

limits: Checkpoint decoding currently allocates before restored rows are detached. JSON snapshot/serialization, spill payload and output projection allocations still require independent admission.
Run payloads remain retained across in-memory runs; maxBufferedRows controls run construction, while the shared allocation cap bounds the retained collection.
Scratch charges are conservative accounting units, not a portable native-sort or total-heap measurement.
